sections.h2: Seven of 17 states budget a deficit above the 3% of GSDP limit

chart.title: Punjab's 4.1% is highest, and all seven budget above the 3% limit
chart.source: PRS Legislative Research, 2026-27 state budget analyses.

sections.means: Seven states budget deficits above 3% of GSDP, led by Punjab at 4.1%.
sections.todo: States above the limit should bring their 2026-27 deficits within the Finance Commission's 3% of GSDP ceiling.

sections.h2: Seven of nine states with revised figures ended 2025-26 above 3%

chart.title: Bihar's revised deficit of 11.8% is the outlier among the nine states
chart.sub: Deficit for 2025-26, % of GSDP: budget estimates versus revised figures as reported.
chart.source: PRS Legislative Research, 2026-27 state budget analyses.

sections.means: Bihar's revised figure is 11.8% after spending excluding debt repayment ran 36% above budget.
sections.todo: Budget plans should be judged against revised outturns, since seven of the nine states overshot their 2025-26 targets.

sections.h2: Interest takes 20% or more of revenue in Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Haryana

chart.title: Punjab's 23% interest share is the highest, Bihar's 9% the lowest
chart.source: PRS Legislative Research budget analyses; Gujarat derived from its budget table.

sections.means: Punjab spends 23% of its revenue receipts on interest, and Bihar spends 9%.
sections.todo: States where interest already takes 20% or more of revenue should show how they will meet the 3% limit.

sections.h2: Counting the Centre's 50-year loans adds 0.4 points to states' deficits

chart.title: Excluding the 50-year loans makes states' 2025-26 deficit 0.4 points smaller

sections.means: Combined states' deficit is 3.2% of GSDP with the SASCI loans and 2.8% without them, a 0.4-point gap.
sections.todo: Deficit reporting should count the SASCI loans, because the money is still borrowed and has to be repaid.
